subject.title: [Feature]: Stop Burying Your Agent's Soul: Configurable Context File Elevation

question: Should special bootstrap-file elevation and Project Context exclusion become a narrow core config surface, or should OpenClaw expose it through a plugin/context-engine prompt contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the accepted surface affects public config, prompt authority, plugin boundaries, prompt-cache stability, and overlapping context-control proposals, so automation should not pick the product/API contract.

options.title: Extend context-engine or plugin contract
options.body: Add or document the minimal prompt/context API needed to map selected bootstrap files into named higher-priority sections and suppress duplicate Project Context rendering.

options.title: Add narrow core config
options.body: Introduce a typed pattern-to-section/exclusion setting with unchanged defaults, schema/docs/help labels, and tests for ordering, cache boundaries, and missing-file behavior.

options.title: Keep flat Project Context
options.body: Decline the new surface and document the supported hook or prompt-extension workaround for operators who want custom persona handling.

recommendation.title: Extend context-engine or plugin contract
recommendation.body: Add or document the minimal prompt/context API needed to map selected bootstrap files into named higher-priority sections and suppress duplicate Project Context rendering.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent prompt/config history and prior review context make steipete the strongest routing candidate for this product/API boundary.
